claims.text: Charles Lindbergh made the first solo non-stop transatlantic flight, from New York to Paris, in May 1927.
Amelia Earhart flew solo across the Atlantic in 1932, Louis Blériot flew across the English Channel in 1909, and Howard Hughes did not make the 1927 flight.
Lindbergh's flight in the Spirit of St. Louis took about 33.5 hours.
John Alcock and Arthur Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight, as a two-man crew, in 1919.
